name: application-inline-add-row
title: Inline Add Row
description: Table footer row with always-editable inputs for adding a new item without leaving the table, driven by a typed items/draft prop contract.
useWhen: Users frequently add short, simple rows (tasks, tags, line items) and shouldn't need a separate dialog.
The new-item fields are few enough to fit inline in a footer row.
You want the add affordance always visible rather than hidden behind a button that opens a form.
avoidWhen: The new item needs many fields or complex validation — use a Dialog or Drawer form instead of cramming it into a row.
Rows need full inline cell editing after creation too — pair this with a dedicated data-grid cell editor instead.
Table width is too narrow for multiple inline inputs — a modal add-flow avoids layout cramping.
responsiveBehavior: The footer inputs sit in a flex row that wraps if needed on narrow viewports; the task input grows to fill remaining space while the assignee input keeps a fixed width.
accessibility: Both inputs carry visible placeholder text describing their purpose; pair with a visually hidden label if omitting placeholder-only guidance in production.
The Add button is a labeled text button, not icon-only, so its action is unambiguous.
The cancel (clear) button is icon-only but carries an explicit aria-label.

variants.title: Inline Add Row
variants.description: Task table with existing rows and an always-visible footer row containing task-name and assignee inputs, an Add button, and a clear action.
accessibility: The footer row uses colSpan to remain a valid table row while hosting non-cell input controls.

variants.title: Inline Add Row (Dark)
variants.description: Inline add-row table adapted for dark surfaces with the same footer-input and Add/clear action structure.
accessibility: Footer input borders, placeholder text, and the Add button must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
